images.caption: Exterior of the Chicago Children's Museum located on Navy Pier in Chicago

brief: The pier's shore-end hall: a long brick building with twin square towers topped by open belvederes, a big arched central entrance lettered 'Navy Pier', a flagged plaza and fountains in front. Four photos. Older than 1970 (1916): the pier pavilion hall of this type is pre-war. Piles carried 10 m below the modelled bed (spec rule 4).

facade.notes: Navy Pier Headhouse (Chicago, 1916): a long red-brick shore-end hall with twin square towers topped by open lanterns, a great arched centre with a barrel roof lettered 'Navy Pier', stone trim; a plaza with a black granite fountain, lamp posts

why.note: municipal piers (1910s) built as public landmarks: towers seen from the lake and the city
